title: Clippers and Clampers Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav shouts into a cheap microphone and the tops of his voice wave come out cut flat. Circuits can do this on purpose. A clipper cuts off the part of a wave above or below a level (a low ceiling over a jumping kid). A clamper lifts or lowers the whole wave without changing its shape (a trampoline on a stage).

On a live breadboard we build a shunt clipper and watch the oscilloscope: the diode stays off in one half, turns on above 0.7 V and holds the output there. Flip the diode and the other half is cut; add a battery and the clip level becomes VB + 0.7 V. Then a positive clamper: in the first negative half the capacitor charges to the peak, acts like a small battery and lifts every point of the wave, while the peak to peak size stays the same (RC much bigger than T, also called a DC restorer). Worked example: a 5 V peak wave through an ideal positive clamper swings from 0 to 10 V. Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 47 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes.
